rationale: Objective: minimize the max across ranks of per-rank summed NCCL kernel durations for one accumulated step (median of 3 profiled runs), subject to step_ms <= 1.05x baseline. Measured facts on this revision (inputs/observations, exact provenance): the step issues exactly 13 SUM allreduces per rank on process group 0 - 12x 28,351,488 B buckets (call d0938de87369efd500322679) plus 1x 157,541,376 B bucket (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b), totaling the full 497,759,232 B fp32 gradient payload - and every device kernel in both the execution_timeline discovery and the separate nsys run is ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL (grid 2x544, 2 channels), i.e. the low-bandwidth LL protocol. On the same leased, NVLink-less PCIe GPU pair, the warmed-worker nccl_tuning collector logs NCCL's own tuner decision Algo RING proto SIMPLE for precisely these sizes/dtypes (28,351,488 B x24, 157,541,376 B x2, 497,759,232 B x1), an actionable mismatch. Clean collective_calibration at the exact observed sizes gives ~1.995 ms per 27 MiB bucket and ~10.65 ms for the 150 MiB bucket, matching the late-arriving rank's in-step LL kernel durations: the step sits at the LL floor (~34.5 ms/rank) and the residual gap to the ~38.09 ms baseline objective is inter-rank arrival skew paid as in-kernel waiting. Hypotheses, explicitly not facts: (a) LL's flag-interleaved packets cost roughly half of achievable bandwidth at these sizes, so a SIMPLE-pinned communicator should roughly halve per-byte kernel time (~2.0 -> ~1.0-1.2 ms per 27 MiB bucket, ~10.6 -> ~5.5-6.5 ms for the 150 MiB bucket, max-rank sum toward ~19-24 ms); (b) no collector establishes why the in-step communicator selected LL while a warmed worker selects SIMPLE, and no timed SIMPLE sample at these sizes exists yet; (c) protocol choice does not remove arrival skew, which may keep the max-rank sum above the single-rank floor. This attempt implements the selected joint hypothesis with minimal semantic surface: at build time both ranks create one extra NCCL process group over all ranks (device_id-bound, 600 s timeout) with NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE scoped around the group's communicator initialization (env saved, set, forced by a 4-byte warmup allreduce plus work.wait and cuda.synchronize so later lazy init cannot re-read the restored environment, then restored; the already-initialized default and gloo control communicators are unaffected because NCCL reads these variables at communicator init). The warmup also captures the group's dispatcher custom-class handle through a transient TorchDispatchMode, so no setup work, extra dispatch or extra collective remains inside any invocation. Each replacement then performs exactly ONE c10d::allreduce_ execution per invocation: the parent reference called with the caller's own tensors, ReduceOp, sparse_indices, async_op and timeout, with only the ProcessGroup argument substituted by the fast group; nothing is deferred, fused, grouped, staged or eliminated, and the (tensors, Work) contract, in-place bucket reduction, stream ordering and gradient_as_bucket_view aliasing are inherited from the parent path. Correctness argument: the reduction stays a 2-rank SUM over the same world with the same inputs, so every output element is a single commutative fp32 addition (a[i]+b[i]) regardless of protocol - reduced gradients are bitwise identical to the parent path, preserving the atol=0/rtol=0 exact cross-rank replica check, the serial global-batch reference gradient check, the negative control and the post-step parameter comparison. Both sites are replaced jointly so all 13 collectives move together (replacing one would leave the 10.6 ms embedding bucket on LL and produce mixed reduction paths). Guarded fallbacks: signature-incompatible calls (multi-tensor, non-fp32, non-contiguous, sparse, synchronous, foreign device), single-rank runs and any symmetric setup or capture failure run exact parent passthrough on the caller's own group with retained route labels (fastpg-simple-allreduce, parent-passthrough-signature, parent-passthrough-no-capture, setup-failed:<type>); synchronous originals are passed through as an async parent call whose Work is waited before returning, because a direct Python op call with async_op=false does not execute the collective in this torch build (verified on the worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129). Historical lesson applied (prior-revision trial records at this same boundary): no deferred or grouped launches and no cross-call Work state - the earlier coalescing attempt corrupted only wte.weight on the second continuous step when Works straddled the DDP bucket rebuild; this design is stateless per call and rebuild-safe. Route labels are diagnostic self-report; the protocol switch will be corroborated by the framework's own NCCL kernel evidence (expected ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_SIMPLE entries), not by labels.

steps: dist.new_group(backend='nccl', timeout=600s, device_id=<rank device>) over all ranks: collective store rendezvous plus eager NCCL communicator initialization on both ranks, outside every timed invocation and before quality tracking.

NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE environment variable saved, set around the group's communicator initialization, then restored; the default NCCL communicator and the gloo control group are already initialized and unaffected.

One 4-byte fp32 warmup allreduce on the new group (forces communicator init under the forced protocol and warms its kernels), work.wait() plus torch.cuda.synchronize on the rank device, all inside build.

Transient TorchDispatchMode around that warmup call captures the new group's dispatcher custom-class handle, so per-invocation fast paths are a single parent op call with the group argument substituted (no per-invocation dispatch dance, no extra collectives, verified end-to-end on the worker's torch build with CPU emulation of the dispatch boundary).
setup_work.memory_effects: The extra NCCL communicator allocates channel/send-recv buffers via driver allocations outside PyTorch's pools: not reflected in peak_allocated/lifecycle_peak_allocated counters, but it does increase retained driver memory for the worker lifetime. PyTorch-side setup allocation is one 4-byte tensor (freed). No model parameters are transformed; no CUDA graphs are captured.
setup_work.lifecycle: The group and its handle persist for the worker process across warmup, repeats, continuous steps and the 3 profiled diagnostic runs; per-invocation behavior after the first is a stateless parent-call substitution.

quality_risks: The SIMPLE-protocol timing at the exact bucket sizes is a hypothesis: no timed SIMPLE sample at 28,351,488/157,541,376 B exists in the observations; if SIMPLE is not faster than LL here, the objective may not improve, though semantics remain bitwise-parent and step_ms is unaffected aside from kernel durations.

Why the in-step default communicator selects LL while the warmed worker's tuner selects SIMPLE is not established by any collector; if the in-step LL choice is driven by a condition that also applies to the fresh group's communicator despite the forced protocol, the fast path degenerates toward baseline-equivalent behavior rather than failure.
Residual inter-rank arrival skew is paid inside NCCL kernel durations in both protocols; the max-rank sum can stay above the late-arriving rank's floor even after a successful protocol switch.

The ReduceOp arrives as an opaque custom-class object and cannot be inspected from Python; the fast path executes the caller's own ReduceOp unchanged through the parent, and every observed collective at these two sites is SUM (DDP's reducer hardcodes SUM), but a hypothetical non-SUM async fp32 call would also be routed to the fast group - still a same-world SUM-equivalent reduction with the caller's own operator, so only transport changes.
If NCCL ignores NCCL_PROTO for the fresh communicator, kernels remain tuner-selected (observed LL) and the candidate is baseline-equivalent, not incorrect.

Asymmetric runtime failure mid-collective could hang the pair (inherent to any distributed rewrite); mitigations: setup validation is deterministic and symmetric on both ranks, every fallback decision is made before any enqueue (pure function of the local signature), and no post-enqueue fallback exists.
The extra 4-byte warmup allreduce and the group creation run once at installation; if the evaluator ever re-enters build, one additional group would be created per re-entry (leaked but harmless).
